title: DIC, Liver Disease and Fibrinolysis: Consumption vs Rebalance
summary: Understand plasmin, its brakes and D-dimer; score overt DIC with the ISTH system and manage it by treating the cause; recognise the rebalanced hemostasis of cirrhosis; and use the reptilase time to spot heparin.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 36 Hits 3, 10, 11, 14, 15 and 18 and Traps 3 and 6. Checked against Iba 2023, Wada 2014 (four DIC guidelines and the ISTH harmonization), Lisman & Porte 2017, Medcalf & Keragala 2021, Reardon 2026 and Besser & MacDonald 2016. Hit 14 and Trap 6 say platelets > 20 × 10⁹/L in bleeding DIC; the guidelines summarized by Wada 2014 transfuse bleeding patients at ≤ 50 × 10⁹/L (register flag rv-dic-platelets). Not taught: D-dimer as an FXIIIa cross-link neo-epitope, low-dose heparin 3–5 IU/kg/h, vitamin K dose and onset (Trap 5), dysfibrinogenemia prolonging both TT and reptilase, VWF 300–600%, and the INR > 3 figure.

objectives: Describe plasminogen activation, the brakes on fibrinolysis and what D-dimer represents.
Calculate an ISTH overt DIC score and state when it applies.
Explain DIC management priorities and component thresholds.
Explain rebalanced hemostasis in cirrhosis and interpret a long thrombin time with a normal reptilase time.

scenes.title: Two long PTs, two different problems
scenes.altText: Two patient cards. Patient A: septic shock; platelets 42 × 10⁹/L, D-dimer strongly raised, PT prolonged 7 s, fibrinogen 85 mg/dL; oozing from line sites. Patient B: stable cirrhosis before a paracentesis; INR 2.5, platelets 70 × 10⁹/L, no bleeding. A request slip on B: “FFP before procedure?” The cartoon scientist compares the two coag panels.

cues.text: Patient A is in septic shock, oozing from every line. Platelets 42, D-dimer sky-high, PT seven seconds long, fibrinogen 85.
Patient B has stable cirrhosis and needs a paracentesis. INR 2.5, platelets 70, no bleeding. Someone asks for plasma first.
Both have a long PT. One is consuming clotting factors; the other is rebalanced. The lab can tell them apart.

scenes.title: Clot, then controlled lysis
scenes.altText: A schematic fibrin mesh forms (thrombin → fibrin). Plasminogen docks on lysine sites on fibrin; tPA and uPA activate it to plasmin, which digests fibrin and fibrinogen into degradation products; D-dimer is the fragment that comes specifically from clot (fibrin) breakdown. Three brake tokens: PAI-1 (and PAI-2) inhibit tPA and uPA; α2-antiplasmin controls plasmin; TAFI, a carboxypeptidase, removes the lysine docking sites so plasminogen cannot assemble. A note: normal D-dimer is typically < 500 ng/mL FEU, and it rises in VTE and DIC but also in pregnancy, trauma and cancer.

cues.text: Thrombin turns fibrinogen into a fibrin mesh. Clearing that clot is the job of the fibrinolytic system.
Plasminogen docks on lysine sites on fibrin. Tissue and urokinase plasminogen activators turn it into plasmin, which digests fibrin and fibrinogen.
D-dimer is the degradation product that comes specifically from breaking down a clot, so it is more useful for thrombosis than other fragments.
Three brakes keep lysis in check. PAI-1 inhibits the plasminogen activators. Alpha-2-antiplasmin controls plasmin itself. TAFI clips off the lysine docking sites.
D-dimer is usually below 500 nanograms per millilitre FEU. It rises in venous thrombosis and DIC, but also in pregnancy, trauma and cancer.

props.title: D-dimer reading
lines: ↑ VTE, DIC — and pregnancy, trauma, cancer

scenes.title: DIC: scoring consumption
scenes.altText: An ISTH overt DIC scoring card builds, only for a patient with an underlying disorder known to cause DIC. Platelets: ≥ 100 = 0; 50–<100 = 1; < 50 = 2. Fibrin marker (D-dimer): no rise = 0; moderate = 2; strong = 3 (local assay cut-offs). PT prolongation: < 3 s = 0; 3–<6 s = 1; ≥ 6 s = 2. Fibrinogen: ≥ 100 mg/dL = 0; < 100 = 1. Total ≥ 5 = overt DIC. Patient A is scored: platelets 42 → 2; D-dimer strong → 3; PT +7 s → 2; fibrinogen 85 → 1; total 8. A note: fibrinogen < 100 mg/dL by itself prolongs PT and APTT.

cues.text: DIC is systemic clotting that consumes platelets and factors. The ISTH score is used only when an underlying cause, such as sepsis, is present.
Platelets below 100 score one; below 50 score two. A moderate D-dimer rise scores two and a strong rise three, using local cut-offs.
PT prolonged 3 to 6 seconds scores one, 6 or more scores two. Fibrinogen below 100 milligrams per decilitre scores one. A total of 5 or more is overt DIC.
Patient A: platelets 42, two. Strong D-dimer, three. PT plus seven, two. Fibrinogen 85, one. Total eight: overt DIC.
And a fibrinogen this low lengthens the PT and APTT by itself, because there is too little substrate to clot.

props.label: Only with an underlying cause (e.g., sepsis)

scenes.title: Treat the cause; correct only what bleeds
scenes.altText: A management card for DIC (guidelines harmonized by ISTH, as summarized by Wada 2014): treat the underlying disease — the cornerstone. Platelets: transfuse in bleeding DIC at ≤ 50 × 10⁹/L; 10–20 × 10⁹/L for non-bleeding patients after chemotherapy. Plasma (initial 15 mL/kg) for bleeding with PT/APTT > 1.5 × normal; fibrinogen concentrate or cryoprecipitate for low fibrinogen in massive bleeding. A cirrhosis card: PT/APTT measure only procoagulants; both pro- and anticoagulant factors fall, VWF and FVIII rise, and thrombin generation with thrombomodulin is normal or increased — rebalanced. Prophylactic plasma adds volume, raising portal and central venous pressure. A reptilase card: thrombin time prolonged with normal reptilase (heparin-insensitive) points to heparin contamination. Back to the hook: A gets source control plus components for bleeding; B gets no prophylactic plasma for the INR.

cues.text: In DIC, treating the underlying disease is the cornerstone. Blood components are for bleeding, or for high-risk procedures, not for numbers alone.

Guidelines transfuse platelets in bleeding DIC at 50 or below. A lower threshold, 10 to 20, applies to non-bleeding patients after chemotherapy. Plasma and fibrinogen replacement are for bleeding patients.

Cirrhosis is different. The PT measures only procoagulant factors, but anticoagulant proteins fall too, while VWF and factor VIII rise. Thrombin generation with thrombomodulin is normal or even increased.
Plasma given to fix the INR adds volume and raises portal pressure, which can make procedure bleeding worse. The INR is not the patient’s bleeding risk.
One more clue: a long thrombin time with a normal reptilase time means heparin in the sample, because reptilase ignores heparin.

props.label: TT long + reptilase normal → heparin in the sample

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Cirrhotic with INR 2.5 needs FFP before a procedure” (✓ rebalanced hemostasis; plasma raises portal pressure); “Correct every DIC lab value” (✓ treat the cause; components for bleeding or high risk); “Keep platelets > 20 in bleeding DIC” (✓ guidelines transfuse at ≤ 50 when bleeding; 10–20 is for non-bleeding).

cues.text: Trap one: a cirrhotic with an INR of 2.5 needs plasma before a procedure. The hemostasis is rebalanced, and plasma raises portal pressure.
Trap two: correct every DIC lab value. Treat the cause; give components to patients who bleed or face high-risk procedures.
Trap three: keep platelets above 20 in bleeding DIC. Guidelines transfuse a bleeding patient at 50 or below; 10 to 20 is the non-bleeding threshold.

props.title: ✗ “Correct every DIC lab value.”
lines: ✓ Treat the cause; components for bleeding

scenes.title: Five means DIC; the liver is a seesaw
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Five means DIC — but fix the fire, not the numbers. The cirrhotic liver is a seesaw, not a sinking boat.” A score token reaching 5, a fire token, a level seesaw token. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: five means DIC, but fix the fire, not the numbers. And the cirrhotic liver is a seesaw, not a sinking boat.

Where it breaks: the score only applies with an underlying cause; the seesaw is unstable and can tip toward bleeding or clotting; and DIC from leukemia or obstetric causes may need targeted treatment.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “ISTH overt DIC ≥ 5 (platelets, D-dimer, PT, fibrinogen) · treat the cause · bleeding: platelets ≤ 50”, “Cirrhosis: rebalanced — no prophylactic plasma for INR · TT long + reptilase normal = heparin”.

cues.text: Score DIC only when a cause is present, treat that cause and give components to bleeding patients; in cirrhosis, the INR does not measure bleeding risk.

props.label: ISTH DIC ≥ 5 · treat the cause · bleeding: platelets ≤ 50 × 10⁹/L
Cirrhosis rebalanced: no plasma for INR · TT ↑ + reptilase normal = heparin

explanation.what: Plain language: in DIC the body clots everywhere and uses up platelets and clotting factors; in cirrhosis both clotting and anti-clotting proteins fall together, so a long PT overstates bleeding risk. Scientific terms: plasminogen, tPA/uPA, PAI-1, α2-antiplasmin, TAFI, D-dimer, ISTH overt DIC score, rebalanced hemostasis, thrombin generation with thrombomodulin, reptilase (batroxobin) time.
explanation.why: DIC consumes platelets and fibrinogen and generates fibrin that plasmin breaks down (D-dimer). PT and APTT detect only procoagulant deficits; in liver disease, protein C, protein S and antithrombin also fall while VWF and FVIII rise. Reptilase clots fibrinogen directly and is not inhibited by heparin.
explanation.measure: ISTH overt DIC (with an underlying cause): platelets < 100 = 1, < 50 = 2; fibrin marker moderate = 2, strong = 3; PT prolongation 3–< 6 s = 1, ≥ 6 s = 2; fibrinogen < 100 mg/dL = 1; ≥ 5 = overt. Platelet transfusion: bleeding DIC ≤ 50 × 10⁹/L; non-bleeding post-chemotherapy 10–20 × 10⁹/L. Plasma 15 mL/kg initial for bleeding with PT/APTT > 1.5 × normal. D-dimer typically < 500 ng/mL FEU.
explanation.differs: DIC (consumption: low platelets, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, bleeding or clotting) vs cirrhosis (rebalanced: long PT with normal or increased thrombin generation). Heparin contamination (TT long, reptilase normal) vs fibrinogen problems (reptilase also affected).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: D-dimer meaning, ISTH score calculation, “treat the cause,” platelet thresholds, no prophylactic plasma in cirrhosis, and TT vs reptilase.

mnemonic.text: Five means DIC — fix the fire, not the numbers; the cirrhotic liver is a seesaw, not a sinking boat.
mnemonic.explanation: An ISTH score ≥ 5 means overt DIC, managed by treating the cause; cirrhosis lowers pro- and anticoagulants together.
mnemonic.limitation: The score applies only with an underlying cause; the cirrhotic balance is unstable and can tip either way; some DIC types need targeted therapy.

analogyLimitations: The fibrin mesh and seesaw are schematic.
The patients and values are invented.
Viscoelastic testing and specific DIC therapies (antithrombin, thrombomodulin) are not covered.
takeaway: Score DIC only when a cause is present, treat that cause and give components to bleeding patients; in cirrhosis, the INR does not measure bleeding risk.

questions.stem: A septic patient has platelets 65 × 10⁹/L, a moderate D-dimer rise, PT prolonged by 4 s and fibrinogen 180 mg/dL. What is the ISTH overt DIC score?

options.rationale: Correct. Platelets 50–<100 = 1, moderate D-dimer = 2, PT +3–<6 s = 1, fibrinogen ≥ 100 = 0; total 4 (< 5).
Incorrect. Fibrinogen 180 scores 0, so the total is 4.

options.text: The score cannot be used in sepsis
options.rationale: Incorrect. Sepsis is a classic underlying cause; the score requires one.

questions.stem: A patient with stable cirrhosis (INR 2.4, platelets 80 × 10⁹/L) is scheduled for paracentesis and is not bleeding. What is the best laboratory-informed advice?

options.text: No prophylactic plasma to correct the INR; hemostasis is rebalanced
options.rationale: Correct. PT/INR misses the fall in anticoagulant proteins; plasma adds volume and raises portal pressure.

options.text: Give FFP until the INR is below 1.5
options.rationale: Incorrect. Correction is often unachievable and can worsen bleeding by raising portal pressure.

options.text: Give vitamin K and delay until the INR normalises
options.rationale: Incorrect. Waiting for the INR to normalise rests on the same mistaken idea that the INR measures bleeding risk in cirrhosis.

options.text: Start heparin because cirrhosis is hypercoagulable
options.rationale: Incorrect. The balance is unstable; there is no indication here.

questions.stem: A sample drawn from a central line has a markedly prolonged thrombin time and a normal reptilase time. What is the most likely explanation?

options.rationale: Correct. Heparin prolongs the thrombin time but not the reptilase time.
Incorrect. Absent fibrinogen would prolong both tests.
Incorrect. The thrombin time bypasses factor VII.
Incorrect. This pattern specifically points to heparin.
